params.body:
From Nightwatch (issue 20), a quarter of an hour after the last deploy: a visitor on his phone was looking at a car on a dealer's website and got a 500 where a photo should have been.

A bucket can answer "I don't know" to "does this file exist", and that is not the same as "no". `Storage::disk('vehicles')->exists()` threw `UnableToCheckFileExistence` for `21433/car_image_90.jpeg` and nothing caught it, so one refused lookup took the whole page down.

Reading the method turned up two more things standing next to that one:

- a photo that genuinely is not there returned `false`, which Laravel renders as an **empty response with status 200** — the browser is told nothing is wrong while an image is missing;
- underneath that `return` stood a `throw new FileNotFoundException()` that could never be reached, importing the `FileNotFoundException` of a crypto library (`phpseclib3`) that has nothing to do with filesystems. An editor's auto-import that never ran.

The whole delivery now sits in a `try`. A response that already says 404 passes through untouched; anything the bucket, the resize or the disk cache throws is logged and becomes a 404. A photo that cannot be delivered is a broken image, never a broken page.

New rule R S2-5.25, and `APhotoTheBucketCannotAnswerForTest` pins the four cases: the bucket refusing the question, a photo that is not there, a hash that decodes to nothing, and a real photo that still comes back as webp. Checked against the unfixed code: the first two failed, the other two passed, which is exactly right.

The PHPStan baseline is one entry shorter — it held the unreachable `throw`.

Fixes bevinding een-foto-die-de-emmer-niet-kan-bevestigen.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: A photo the bucket cannot answer for
